highlights:
# Together cuts Dedicated Inference pricing on H100s to $3.99 per hour

Together says it is lowering the price of Dedicated Inference on H100 GPUs from $5.49 per hour to $3.99 per hour starting in September, with the lower price applied automatically to new and existing deployments. The company says the pricing applies to deployments of models including Gemma 4, Qwen3/3.5, gpt-oss, Llama, and Nemotron 3.5.

Published September 1, 2026 at 1:36 AM CDT Updated September 1, 2026 at 3:00 AM CDT

Why it matters

Lower inference prices can quickly change where teams run production workloads and intensify price competition across AI infrastructure providers.

results.title: Is Together AI Cheaper Than Fireworks AI in 2026? | Markaicode
results.author: Markaicode Editorial
highlights:
- Sources: Together AI's official pricing page and Fireworks AI's official serverless pricing docs, both fetched live on September 4, 2026 [VERIFIED S0]. OpenAI's official API pricing page, same date [VERIFIED S0], used for the Pricing vs Alternatives section only.
- Currency/region: USD, standard (non-batch, non-priority) serverless tier, global routing unless noted.

...

- Known catalog change: Together AI's pricing page no longer lists "Llama 3 8B" (standard) or Mixtral 8x7B/8x22B as named line items; the nearest current equivalents are cited below.

...

Figures marked [derived] are arithmetic computed from S0 rates (e.g., cache-discount percentages, scenario totals) and are not separately vendor-stated. No figure in this article is EDITORIAL S2 or below — where only S2-tier sources existed (e.g., older third-party "negotiated enterprise rate" claims), the number was dropped rather than included with a downgraded label.

...

Fireworks ... - ... appear to ... standalone ... chang ... page ... DeepSeek ... Flash ... below ... corroborated ... independently ... serverless pricing ... and ... model ... than ... source.

...

| Model | Together AI | Fireworks AI | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | $0.14 in / $0.03 cached / $0.28 out [S0] | $0.22 in / $0.007 cached / $0.66 out [S0] | Headline SKU on both platforms; used as this article's baseline. Together's rate is unchanged since the model's Aug 3, 2026 serverless launch, per its official changelog [S0] |
| Llama 3 8B (budget open-weight) | $0.14 / $0.14, "Llama 3 8B Instruct Lite" [S0], raised from $0.10/$0.10 effective May 29, 2026 per Together's changelog [S0] | $0.20 / $0.20, 4B–16B size-tier fallback [S0] | The original "Llama 3 8B Instruct" (non-Lite) SKU was deprecated from Together's serverless catalog on Aug 27, 2025 [S0] — over 9 months before this article's original June 2026 draft was published |
| Mixtral 8x7B (MoE) | Deprecated [S0]: `Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` on Apr 14, 2026; `Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1` (base) on Jul 29, 2026, per Together's official changelog | $0.50 / $0.50, MoE ≤56B size-tier fallback [S0] | Together dropped this model line entirely; Fireworks still serves it under its parameter-based fallback pricing |
| GLM-5.3 (frontier open-weight) | $1.40 in ($0.26 cached) / $4.40 out [S0] | $1.40 in ($0.26 cached) / $4.40 out [S0] | Identical published rate on both platforms |
| Dedicated H100 (per GPU-hour) | $5.49 list, $3.99 promo (expires 09/30/26) [S0] | $8.00 (effective Sep 1, 2026; was $7.00) [S0] | Billed separately from token pricing |

...

## Hidden Costs Developers Miss

1. Model catalog churn — Llama 3 8B "standard" and Mixtral 8x7B/8x22B are no longer named line items on Together AI's pricing page; anyone budgeting off an older article citing those exact SKUs needs to remap to current equivalents.
2. Fireworks' Sep 1, 2026 GPU price step-up — on-demand H100 rose from $7.00 to $8.00/hour, and B200 from $10.00 to $13.00/hour, already in effect as of this writing.
3. Together's dedicated H100 promo expiry — the $3.99/hour rate is explicitly marked as valid only until 09/30/26; the list price reverts to $5.49/hour afterward.
4. Cached-input asymmetry — Fireworks discounts cached input by ~97% ($0.22 → $0.007) versus Together's ~79% ($0.14 → $0.03) for this model; the platform that looks cheaper can flip for cache-heavy workloads at some volumes even though it doesn't at the scale modeled below.
5. Fireworks region-restricted premium — dedicated deployments locked to a specific region carry a stated 1.5x price premium.
6. Fireworks US-only serverless premium — as of September 1, 2026, US-only-routed serverless models are priced 50% above the global rate.
7. Fine-tuning minimums — Together AI's standard fine-tuning jobs carry a $4.00 minimum charge per job regardless of dataset size; per-model minimums for larger models run higher.

...

- Security: Private/dedicated deployment is priced separately from serverless on both platforms (see the H100 GPU-hour row above); there is no discounted "private" token rate on either vendor's public pricing page [S0].
- Compliance: Fireworks charges a stated 1.5x premium for region-restricted dedicated deployments and a 50% premium on US-only-routed serverless models as of Sep 1, 2026 [S0]. Together's pricing page does not list an equivalent region/compliance surcharge for the models compared here — not verified as offering region-locked serverless at standard rates; confirm directly with sales if data residency is a requirement.
- Ops: Neither platform charges an idle fee on serverless (you only pay for tokens sent) [S0]; idle cost only applies once you move to dedicated GPU-hour billing, which bills continuously whether or not it's handling traffic.
- Cost honesty: Together's $3.99/hour dedicated H100 rate is explicitly marked as a promotion expiring 09/30/26, reverting to $5.49/hour list price afterward [S0] — budget off the list price for anything extending past that date.
- Procurement: Neither vendor publishes a negotiated high-volume or annual-commitment rate for the models in this article; Together's Provisioned Throughput product (reserved token capacity, one-month minimum term) is a real self-serve commitment option [S0], while Fireworks' equivalent (Reserved Throughput) requires contacting sales directly [S0]. Treat any "enterprise discount %" figure you see elsewhere as unverified unless it cites one of these two products by name.

results.title: Together AI Pricing (2026): PTUs Buy Capacity, Not Savings | Omid Saffari
results.author: Omid Saffari
highlights:
Every price and limit on this page was verified against Together AI's live pricing page, billing documentation, and product documentation on August 22, 2026. That date matters. The current page already differs materially from June pricing coverage: it lists MiniMax M3, Kimi K3, GLM-5.2, lower live dedicated hardware rates, and the new Provisioned Throughput layer.

...

Dedicated Inference is the right move when control matters more than self-serve flexibility. Together allocates single-tenant hardware, supports custom models, and offers autoscaling and traffic-spike handling. The live price is $5.49 per GPU-hour for an NVIDIA HGX H100 and $8.99 for an HGX B200. H200, B300, GB200 NVL72, and GB300 NVL72 prices require sales contact.

...

GPU clusters hand more of the stack to the buyer. The current on-demand rates are $3.99 per GPU-hour for H100, $5.99 for H200, and $8.19 for B200. A 30-day H100 equivalent is $2,872.80, but that is not a cheaper substitute for the $3,952.80 Dedicated H100. The cluster buyer owns more deployment, serving, orchestration, observability, and utilization work.

Reserved cluster rates decrease with commitment.

...

:::faq-item{q="Did Together AI pricing change in 2026?"}
Yes. Together AI launched Provisioned Throughput on July 8, 2026, adding reserved token capacity at $0.05 per PTU-minute, a one-month minimum, and a 99% uptime SLA. The current serverless catalog and dedicated hardware rates have also moved since June, which is why this page carries an August 22 verification date.

...

PTUs buy reserved capacity and an SLA; a negotiated commitment discount can improve the rate, but Together does not publish that schedule.

The dedicated-inference premium is the number people miss. That is a reasonable price for not operating it yourself, but it must be in the model.

results.title: Together AI Cuts GPU Cluster Pricing in Half for Interruptible Workloads | Superpower Daily
results.author: Superpower Daily Editorial Desk
highlights:
The public preview gives checkpointed jobs a cheaper way to scale, while putting reliability work—and the risk of sudden capacity loss—on customers.

By Superpower Daily Editorial Desk Published Sep 10, 2026, 5:09 PM PDT 2 min read

Together AI Cuts GPU Cluster Pricing in Half for Interruptible Workloads

 Read transcript

Together AI is opening a public preview that cuts the price of certain GPU capacity in half. Its new preemptible option runs NVIDIA GPU nodes at 50% of the on-demand rate, using spare capacity for workloads that can tolerate interruption. The trade-off is straightforward: Together can reclaim those nodes when it needs the capacity elsewhere. Affected Kubernetes pods receive a termination signal and get up to five minutes to checkpoint—that is, save enough progress to resume later—and exit before the node disappears. Together says the rate is fixed, rather than changing like a spot-market price, and usage is measured roughly every one to two minutes, so short jobs are billed for approximately the time they actually run. This works inside a normal Together GPU Cluster, not as a separate cluster. Customers must keep at least one standard node, while preemptible nodes can be added to new or existing clusters. Together can refill the requested preemptible capacity as spare capacity returns, but that target is not a reservation: live allocation may fall below it, and there is no minimum node lifetime. The model fits experiments, evaluations, fine-tuning, distillation, batch inference, and other restartable work. It is a poor match for multi-day jobs without checkpoints or strict serving without fallback. Kubernetes is supported in every region for now; Slurm, more regions, and in-place conversion are planned. The key constraint is whether a team’s software can make a sudden GPU loss routine instead of disruptive.

...

Together AI has opened a public preview of preemptible compute for its GPU Clusters, offering NVIDIA GPU nodes at a flat half of the on-demand price. The trade is direct: teams can cut costs for restartable work, but Together can reclaim that capacity when it needs it elsewhere.

The preview is available on Kubernetes clusters in all regions and can be added to new or existing Together GPU Clusters. Rather than creating a separate cluster, the discounted nodes join an existing one alongside standard nodes, which Together says are fulfilled synchronously and are never preempted.

...

Preemptible nodes draw from unused capacity on the same NVIDIA accelerated-computing infrastructure. They are billed sub-hourly, with usage measured about every one to two minutes, so a short-lived worker is charged for roughly the time it runs rather than a full hour.

...

Together says the rate is fixed at half the on-demand price rather than changing with a spot market. When capacity is reclaimed, workloads have up to five minutes to save progress and exit before the node is removed.

results.title: Signals: token myths, quant maps, and cheaper GPU hours
results.author: The Signal Desk
highlights: Together AI launched preemptible GPU compute in public preview on September 10, 2026: a flat 50% discount off its on-demand rates, billed every 1-2 minutes, with a 5-minute SIGTERM drain before reclaim. It targets ablations, sweeps, quick fine-tunes and batch inference, jobs that can checkpoint and restart without drama. The discount lands on top of a market already softening: Ornn Data’s index had an H100 SXM at $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26, down 8.5% in a week (see /gpu/). Credit: Ornn Data.
